definitions.explanation: The academic study of human history and prehistory through the excavation and analysis of physical remains such as artifacts, structures, and other material evidence.

examples.japanese: {考古学|こうこがく}を{学|まな}ぶ。
{大学|だいがく}で{考古学|こうこがく}を{専攻|せんこう}している。
examples.english: I am majoring in archaeology at university.

examples.japanese: {考古学|こうこがく}の{発掘調査|はっくつちょうさ}で{貴重|きちょう}な{土器|どき}が{見|み}つかった。
examples.english: Valuable pottery was found during an archaeological excavation.

notes:
The academic discipline of studying ancient civilizations through physical evidence. Composed of {考|こう} (consider) + {古|こ} (ancient) + {学|がく} (study/science).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {考古学|こうこがく}の{発掘|はっくつ}: archaeological excavation
- {考古学|こうこがく}を{専攻|せんこう}する: to major in archaeology
- {考古学|こうこがく}{調査|ちょうさ}: archaeological survey
- {考古学的|こうこがくてき}{発見|はっけん}: archaeological discovery
- {考古学者|こうこがくしゃ}: archaeologist

RELATED WORDS:
- {歴史学|れきしがく}: history (as an academic discipline) — uses written records rather than physical remains
- {人類学|じんるいがく}: anthropology — broader study of human societies and cultures
- {古代|こだい}: ancient times — a time period that archaeology often focuses on
